source.title: A practical generalization metric for deep networks benchmarking
source.authors: Meng-Qing Huang; Hongchuan Yu; Jianjun Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures generalization-related outcomes across pretrained model families and compares them with theoretical estimates, using its own benchmark and metric. It does not test any claim version's specified intervention or measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for its benchmarked model groups and datasets. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected networks, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks pretrained CLIP and EfficientNet using a proposed trade-off metric and checks unspecified complexity measures against error-rate rankings. It does not test any of V1–V8. Parameter-count comparisons do not isolate width beyond interpolation, and the consistency analysis does not identify magnitude-aware sharpness or test its specified relationship with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors propose a practical trade-off metric and benchmark, report misalignment between existing complexity estimates and their measurements, and acknowledge coverage limited to CNN-based CLIP and EfficientNet. Their reliability claim concerns their proposed metric; the study does not establish a verdict on V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained models fine-tuned with a linear probe and a practical trade-off metric; it does not reproduce the original methods in the listed sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the comparison: the CLIP generalization bound is higher than EfficientNet's on ImageNet and lower on CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: Selected trade-off generalization-bound values are 0.364 versus 0.206 for CLIP versus EfficientNet on ImageNet, and 0.852 versus 0.902 on CIFAR-100.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The ordering of pretrained model families on this proposed metric can depend on the dataset and selected trade-off conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report sign-error above 0.5 for 30% and 100% of robustness comparisons on ImageNet and CIFAR-100, respectively, versus 43% and 21% for zero-shot comparisons.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Agreement between the evaluated complexity measures and this benchmark's error-rate rankings depends on the dataset and evaluation dimension.

record.code_released: not stated; the supplied text gives an abbreviated URL (https://...)
record.problems: The paper is limited to CLIP and EfficientNet, uses pretrained models with linear-probe fine-tuning, and reports no uncertainty for the trade-off values. The reported metric is not the direct training-test gap used in the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional benchmark rows extracted. The paper's other reported trade-off dimensions (diversity, SSIM, zero-shot percentage, and model size) do not directly measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out generalization.
Widening networks beyond the zero-training-error threshold. The parameter-count comparisons also vary architecture and do not establish interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.

Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps among similarly fitted networks, including comparison with norm and margin measures. The 23 evaluated measures are not individually identified in the supplied text.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T2 classification conflicts with its own finding that no claim version is tested. Generalization terminology and citations alone do not establish a test. No additional results bearing on a listed version were identified.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison with natural-label generalization.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold; models are pretrained and evaluated after linear-probe fine-tuning.
No fully connected image models or comparison isolating local connectivity.
The paper compares theoretical estimates with its practical measurements, but does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or the specified norm- and margin-based measures on the specified settings.
No removal of memorized training examples.
